verdict.rationale: Convex's docs say you can run the open-source backend on your own servers, using the same up-to-date code as the cloud service. The GitHub repo documents Docker (recommended) or prebuilt-binary deployment, works with Postgres, SQLite, RDS, Fly.io and other tools, and offers a flag to disable telemetry. missing for 10: independent or hands-on community corroboration of running self-hosted Convex in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: you can run the Convex backend on your own servers. Self-hosted Convex runs the open-source backend, and contains the same fully up-to-date code the cloud service uses.
You can either use Docker (recommended) or a prebuilt binary to self host Convex.
Self-hosted Convex works well with a variety of tools including Neon, Fly.io, Vercel, Netlify, RDS, Sqlite, Postgres, and more.
if you really want to disable it, you can set the --disable-beacon flag on the backend binary.
